---
title: "Week 14: CLI applications"
---

## Introduction

This week turns Rust programs into command-line tools. We start the way Rust Book chapter 12 does, reading arguments by hand with `std::env::args`, then let the `clap` crate build the parser, help screen, and error messages from a struct. Lab 14 brings the Rust weeks together in a tested password generator and validator: modules, enums and `match`, traits, iterators, the `rand` crate, and integration tests that check the program's output.

## Recommended readings

- [Chapter 12: An I/O Project: Building a Command Line Program](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch12-00-an-io-project.html) - Rust Book
- [clap derive tutorial](https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) - Argument parsing from structs and enums
- [rand 0.8 documentation](https://docs.rs/rand/0.8/rand/) - The version Lab 14 uses
- [Command Line Applications in Rust](https://rust-cli.github.io/book/) - Optional, from the Rust CLI working group
